findings.claim: Branch and commit framing such as 'Finalize evidence-led landscape manifest' and 'Complete component decisions' can be read as a finalized or global-best catalog.
findings.correction: Describe the catalog as a dated reviewed baseline. 20/20 layers have recorded decisions: 8 retain, 1 adjust and 11 keep_but_compare, each with an open overturning comparison. Selections are scoped supported choices, not universal winners.
findings.evidence: status: "reviewed_baseline"; universal_superiority: "not_established"; "Selected means the supported choice for the stated task and scope; it does not mean universal benchmark winner."

findings.claim: The durable-memory rationale cites 'recovery evidence' without its composition. A reader could take the 52-page restore as 52 curated memories restored, or as retrieval qualification.
findings.correction: State the restore precisely: 52 latest pages matched the backup (1 ordinary decision and 51 System pages), with 0 missing embeddings. Only one semantic-memory query ran, and restore was same-host. Browser wiki search is FTS5, and embedding rows can retain superseded versions (52 then 54). No comparative retrieval superiority is established.
findings.evidence: "52 latest pages include one ordinary decision and 51 System pages, not 52 curated decisions"; "One semantic-memory query ... no broad retrieval benchmark"; restore_latest_pages_equal_to_backup: 52

findings.claim: 'Consolidation' is used for two different mechanisms, which can conflict across memory documents.
findings.correction: Distinguish native Codex task consolidation (generation 9 completed on attempt 1) from ai-memory's internal LLM consolidation, which is disabled. Hourly learning has prior scheduler admission only; no learned-write quality is established.
findings.evidence: Lifecycle doc: "native Codex consolidation", "consolidation generation 9 completed on attempt 1"; alignment receipt: "LLM consolidation remains disabled", llm_status: "disabled"

findings.claim: agents-operations cites 'ACP research acceptance' without the executed policy, so readers may assume read-only enforcement or full DeerFlow acceptance.
findings.correction: DeerFlow acceptance covers one embedded invoke_acp_agent task through Codex ACP 1.12.0. That ACP's 'read-only' mode maps to workspaceWrite with networkAccess=false and approvalPolicy=on-request, so strict filesystem read-only enforcement is not established. The planner, UI, scheduler, hosting and MCP tool calls were not exercised. Usage came from private adapter logs, not DeerFlow output.
findings.evidence: "ACP 1.12.0 mode ID read-only actually maps to workspaceWrite, networkAccess=false, approvalPolicy=on-request"; "Embedded tool invocation, not a complete DeerFlow planner/UI/scheduler or hosted service."

findings.claim: native-clients refers generically to 'application SDKs', which leaves unclear which SDK actually executed.
findings.correction: Name the Codex Python SDK (openai-codex 0.154.0 with openai 3.16.2) as the SDK actually invoked in the workers receipt. Its configured model/provider is verified, but it is not per-request attestation. The OpenAI Agents SDK has no execution evidence in this packet and should be labeled conditional or unexercised.
findings.evidence: packages: {"openai-codex":"0.154.0","native-codex":"0.155.1","openai":"3.16.2",...}; "The SDK invocation is unchanged."; no Agents SDK package listed

findings.claim: The recovery-portability rationale 'Retained clean-prefix installs ... support the native recipe approach' can be read as covering the whole foundation-cpu profile.
findings.correction: The clean userspace install covered RTK, QMD, Repomix, TOON, Codex, Claude Code and two ECC skills. It ran signed-out clients on the existing WSL kernel, did not verify Node's detached signature, and did not lock transitive npm dependencies. foundation-cpu also requires context-mode, ai-memory and mcporter, which that install did not qualify.
findings.evidence: "fresh Linux userspace on the existing WSL kernel. It is not a booted new PC ... or full-foundation deployment"; foundation-cpu component_ids include "context-mode","ai-memory","mcporter"

completed_report.new_pc_readiness: The catalog is usable as a reproducible recipe baseline for a new Linux/WSL2 x86_64 host, and no new-PC acceptance exists yet. The adoption manifest correctly sets historical_acceptance_transfers=false, native_login_on_target_only, no automatic installers, services, model calls or broker orders, and 'second-machine acceptance pending'. Remaining acceptance on the new PC: (1) install the foundation-cpu profile (git, python3, node, npm, uv, codex, claude, qmd, rtk, ai-memory, mcporter, context-mode) through the supported recipes in a fresh prefix, with rollback; (2) native sign-in and tool discovery in both clients; (3) one useful bounded task per client, including an ai-memory capture/query and a QMD search; (4) repository validation and tests. The optional profiles carry separate risks: semantic-rag has a host-specific vLLM pin and needs a GPU, observability starts services, recovery needs independent key recovery, and trading-nautilus is a prerelease that needs its own broker credentials. Each needs its own target qualification only when selected. Cross-platform and complete second-physical-PC acceptance remain unestablished.
limitations: This is a tool-free review of the supplied packet. I did not read files, verify hashes against the repository, run validation or receipt checks, or observe any host. Nothing here is new-PC acceptance.

DeepAgents, Microsoft Agent Framework and the 525-repository catalog coverage are not in the excerpts. I cannot confirm whether the base index includes them. Per the manifest rules, source-only candidates have neither failed nor been adopted.
